input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The new Windows export tool almost certainly writes CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings. `parseStatement` only splits the input on `"\n"`, so each line (including the header) keeps a trailing `"\r"`. That makes the last header column become `"description\r"` instead of `"description"`, so `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.some((c) => !header.includes(c))` fails for `"description"`, and `assertShape` throws `errors.rowShape` for the header line (index 0 → reported as row 1) — exactly matching the report. The fix should normalize/strip `\r` (e.g. handle CRLF when splitting lines) in `src/ingest/parser.ts`.
